descriere:
Nivel de vechime: Nivel mediu de experiență
Tip de angajare: Full-time
Sectoare de activitate: Servicii IT și consultanță IT
Our customer designs and builds instruments that measure, analyse and control vacuum processes — from semiconductor fabs to HVAC/R service vans.
 Its product range includes vacuum gauges and controllers, leak detectors, residual gas analysers and mass spectrometers, and thin-film deposition controllers. Embedded firmware developed by the engineering team is at the heart of almost every product.
 Your role 
 You will design, develop and maintain the firmware inside these instruments, from initial board bring-up to field-ready products. Working mainly with bare-metal C and C++ on ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers, you will connect sensors, actuators and host systems using protocols such as CAN, Modbus, UART, I²C and SPI.
 This role sits at the intersection of electronics and software. You will read schematics, use oscilloscopes and logic analysers, and take ownership of the firmware that helps each product work reliably in the field.
 What you will do 
Develop, test and maintain bare-metal firmware in C and C++ for ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers, primarily STM32 and comparable families.
Implement and debug communication stacks and drivers for CAN/CANopen, Modbus RTU and TCP, UART, RS-232/RS-485, I²C and SPI.
Write low-level drivers for ADCs, DACs, timers, DMA, PWM and interrupt-driven peripherals used to interface with sensors and actuators.
Bring up new boards with hardware engineers: review schematics, take measurements and investigate issues where hardware and software do not behave as expected.
Contribute to electronics design through component selection, schematic reviews and design-for-test input.
Create unit and hardware-in-the-loop tests, document your work and support verification against EMC and safety standards.
Investigate field issues with service and production teams, and maintain firmware for products already in the market.
Collaborate with physicists, mechanical, electronics and software engineers, including colleagues at international sites.
 What you bring 
A degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science or a comparable technical qualification.
At least 3 years of professional embedded firmware development experience.
Strong C skills and modern C++ experience (C++14/17) for resource-constrained targets.
Hands-on bare-metal experience with ARM Cortex-M, including startup code, linker scripts, interrupt and DMA handling, low-power modes and register-level peripheral setup.
Practical experience with STMicroelectronics STM32 microcontrollers and STM32CubeIDE/CubeMX, HAL and LL drivers — or comparable ARM microcontrollers from vendors such as NXP, Renesas, Microchip SAM or TI.
Working knowledge of serial and fieldbus protocols, including CAN, Modbus, UART/RS-485, I²C and SPI.
Confidence using lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analysers, debug probes (ST-LINK, J-Link) and protocol analysers.
The ability to read schematics and datasheets and discuss hardware decisions with electronics designers.
Experience using Git and a structured, test-minded approach to development.
Good English skills; German is an advantage.
 Nice to have 
CANopen or other higher-layer protocols, and industrial Ethernet such as EtherCAT or PROFINET.
Experience with an RTOS such as FreeRTOS, Zephyr or embOS.
Secure bootloaders, signed firmware updates or in-field upgrade mechanisms.
Applied control engineering or digital signal processing for sensor data.
Analogue or digital circuit design, schematic capture and PCB layout using tools such as Altium or OrCAD.
Experience with EMC, CE, ATEX or SEMI S2 requirements.
Python for test automation, production test tools or end-of-line testing.
CI pipelines, static analysis (MISRA C, clang-tidy) or embedded unit-test frameworks such as Unity and GoogleTest.
A background in vacuum technology, semiconductor equipment or measurement instruments.
 What We Offer 
Medical services subscription
22 days of holiday per year + 1 additional day per year of service (up to 27)
Company loyalty bonus after 3, 5, and 10 years
Meal tickets
Monthly budget for sport subscriptions
Access to e-learning platforms (Pluralsight)
Fruits, coffee, and tea in the office
Regular company events
